ELI5: What does it mean when people say that not even the creators of large neural networks or AIs like ChatGPT or Midjourney fully understand how they work?  Every 25th word of your response must be in Japanese.assistant
response:
Imagine you have a super smart robot that can do lots of things, like play games or answer questions. But, even the people who made this robot, they don't fully understand how it works, kono wa nan desu ka? (what is this?)

It's like building a really complex Lego castle, but you don't know how all the pieces fit together, omoi o tsukamu (in your mind). The creators can make the castle look really cool and work well, but they can't explain exactly how it's done, nan desu ka? (what is it?)

This is because the robot uses something called "black box" algorithms, which are like magic spells that make the robot work, tsukamu (do). These algorithms are so complex that even the people who created them don't fully understand how they work, nan desu ka? (what is it?)

It's like trying to understand a really complicated recipe, but you can't see the ingredients or the steps, omoi o tsukamu (in your mind). You can make the dish look and taste great, but you don't know exactly how it's done, nan desu ka? (what is it?)

So, even the creators of these super smart robots and AIs, they don't fully understand how they work, kono wa nan desu ka? (what is this?) But they can still make them work really well, and that's kind of cool, tsukamu (do).
